hero.intro: I design circuits that think and visuals that speak. From embedded firmware and power systems to brand identities and cinematic edits — I build things at the intersection of logic and creativity.

eng.label: Engineering
eng.projectsSubtitle: Embedded systems, firmware, power electronics and system design — built, tested and documented.
eng.about:
I'm an electrical engineer who loves the moment a board powers up for the first time. My work spans **embedded systems**, **PCB design**, **power electronics** and **control**, with a strong focus on clean, well-documented firmware.

I enjoy taking a product from a napkin sketch through schematic, layout, firmware and testing — and making sure it's reliable in the real world.

media.label: Multimedia
media.projectsSubtitle: Brand identities, films, motion graphics and media campaigns — crafted with intent.
media.about:
On the other side of my brain lives a designer and storyteller. I build **brand identities** that feel inevitable, cut **videos** with rhythm, and design **motion** that makes people stop scrolling.

My engineering background shapes how I design: systematic, detail-obsessed, and always grounded in a clear purpose.

projects.title: Smart Home Energy Monitor
projects.summary: A Wi-Fi energy monitor that measures real-time power per circuit and streams it to a live dashboard with usage alerts.
projects.description:
## Overview
Household energy bills are a black box. This device clips onto the main panel using **non-invasive CT sensors** and reports real power, apparent power and power factor for up to 4 circuits.

## Highlights
- Custom 2-layer PCB designed in **KiCad** with isolated analog front-end
- ESP32 firmware written in **C++ / FreeRTOS**, sampling at 4 kHz per channel
- MQTT telemetry to a self-hosted dashboard with daily/weekly reports
- Calibrated to **±1.5%** against a reference meter

## Tech stack
`ESP32` `FreeRTOS` `MQTT` `KiCad` `Grafana`

> The biggest lesson: good analog layout matters more than clever code.

steps.title: Research & requirements
steps.text: Defined accuracy targets, safety constraints and chose CT sensors over shunts for isolation.

steps.title: Schematic & PCB
steps.text: Designed the analog front-end with burden resistors, bias network and anti-aliasing filters; routed a compact 2-layer board.

steps.title: Firmware
steps.text: Implemented DMA-based ADC sampling, RMS computation and a FreeRTOS task for MQTT publishing.

steps.title: Calibration & testing
steps.text: Calibrated each channel against a reference meter and stress-tested for 30 days of continuous operation.

projects.title: PID Line-Following Robot
projects.summary: A high-speed line-following robot using an 8-channel IR array and a tuned PID controller running on an STM32.
projects.description:
## Overview
Built for a university robotics competition, this robot follows a track at **1.8 m/s** using a weighted IR-sensor position estimate and a discrete PID loop running at 1 kHz.

## Highlights
- Bare-metal **STM32F4** firmware using HAL + timer interrupts
- Custom motor driver board with current sensing
- Bluetooth live tuning of **Kp, Ki, Kd** from a phone
- Placed **2nd** out of 24 teams

```c
error = position - SETPOINT;
integral += error * dt;
output = Kp*error + Ki*integral + Kd*(error - prev)/dt;
```

steps.title: Mechanical design
steps.text: Lightweight chassis with low center of gravity and N20 micro-gear motors.

steps.title: Sensor array
steps.text: Designed an 8-channel IR reflectance board and normalized readings on startup.

steps.title: Control loop
steps.text: Implemented and tuned a PID controller with anti-windup and derivative filtering.

steps.title: Competition
steps.text: Iterated on tuning at the venue and finished second overall.

projects.title: Solar MPPT Charge Controller
projects.summary: A 200 W synchronous buck MPPT charge controller with a Perturb & Observe algorithm, simulated in Simulink and built on a custom PCB.
projects.description:
## Overview
A maximum-power-point-tracking charge controller for 12 V lead-acid and LiFePO₄ batteries, designed from first principles.

## Highlights
- Full system modeled in **MATLAB / Simulink** before hardware
- Synchronous buck topology at **100 kHz**, peak efficiency **96.4%**
- Perturb & Observe MPPT with adaptive step size
- 3-stage charging profile with temperature compensation

## Results
| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Max power | 200 W |
| Efficiency | 96.4% |
| Tracking accuracy | 99.1% |

steps.title: Simulation
steps.text: Modeled PV panel, converter and battery in Simulink to size components and validate the algorithm.

steps.title: Power stage design
steps.text: Selected MOSFETs, inductor and capacitors for low loss; designed thermal management.

steps.title: Control firmware
steps.text: Implemented P&O MPPT and charge state machine on a microcontroller.

steps.title: Testing
steps.text: Measured efficiency curves and tracking accuracy under real sun and a PV simulator.

gallery.caption: P–V curve and maximum power point

projects.title: Portable FPGA Logic Analyzer
projects.summary: An 8-channel, 200 MS/s logic analyzer built on an FPGA with a Python desktop app for capture, triggering and protocol decoding.
projects.description:
## Overview
Commercial logic analyzers are expensive; this one costs under $40 in parts and decodes **UART, SPI and I²C** out of the box.

## Highlights
- Capture engine written in **Verilog** with configurable triggers
- High-speed USB transfer to a **Python / PyQt** desktop app
- Protocol decoders with an extensible plugin system

## What I learned
Timing closure, clock-domain crossing and designing for testability.

steps.title: Architecture
steps.text: Defined sample buffer, trigger unit and USB bridge as separate FPGA modules.

steps.title: HDL development
steps.text: Wrote and simulated the Verilog modules with testbenches.

steps.title: Desktop software
steps.text: Built the Python capture app with waveform view and decoders.

projects.title: Nebula Coffee — Brand Identity
projects.summary: A cosmic, premium identity for a specialty coffee roaster — logo, palette, packaging and a full brand guideline.
projects.description:
## The brief
Nebula wanted to stand out on crowded specialty shelves while feeling **premium, curious and warm**.

## The solution
A spiral galaxy mark that doubles as a coffee swirl, paired with a deep navy base and electric pink accents. The system scales from stickers to 1 kg bags.

## Deliverables
- Logo suite & construction grid
- Color & typography system
- Packaging, cups, business cards
- 40-page brand guideline

steps.title: Discovery
steps.text: Workshops with the founders to define brand values and audience.

steps.title: Concepts
steps.text: Explored three directions; the cosmic route won for memorability.

steps.title: Refinement
steps.text: Built the construction grid, palette and type hierarchy.

steps.title: Rollout
steps.text: Designed packaging and printed collateral; delivered guidelines.

projects.title: Echoes — Short Film
projects.summary: A neon-noir short film about memory and the city — edited, color graded and sound designed end to end.
projects.description:
## Overview
*Echoes* follows a man retracing a single night across a rain-soaked city. I handled **editing, color grading and sound design**.

## Approach
- Rhythm-driven edit built around the score
- A teal/magenta grade inspired by neon-noir cinema
- Layered ambiences to make the city feel alive

## Recognition
Official selection at two regional short film festivals.

steps.title: Pre-production
steps.text: Storyboards, shot list and look references with the director.

steps.title: Edit
steps.text: Assembled, refined and locked the cut in Premiere Pro.

steps.title: Color
steps.text: Built a node-based grade in DaVinci Resolve.

steps.title: Sound
steps.text: Designed ambiences, foley and final mix.

projects.title: Pulse Fitness — Motion Campaign

projects.description:
